newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SWEDISH INTERNATIONAL BROLIN COULD PLAY FOR LEEDS AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SWEDISH INTERNATIONAL BROLIN COULD PLAY FOR LEEDS AGAIN.

text.p: Leeds United's Swedish international Tomas Brolin, who never settled at the club under former coach Howard Wilkinson, could play for Leeds again now that Wilkinson has been replaced by George Graham.
Brolin, 26, is currently on loan with FC Zurich, but his agent Lars Peterson said on Thursday Brolin could play for the club again following Graham's recent appointment as manager.

Brolin joined Leeds from Italian outfit Parma 10 months ago for 4.5 million pounds ($7.01 million) but fell out with Wilkinson following a series of bust-ups, which culminated in the star refusing to attend pre-season training with the club.
He vowed he would never play for Leeds again and so was loaned out FC Zurich, but Wilkinson's sacking and Graham's subsequent arrival, has led to an apparent change-of-heart.

United also have a striker crisis, with Ghanaian international Tony Yeboah, Brian Deane, captain Ian Rush and on-loan Mark Hateley all hit with injuries, which forced Graham to play Rod Wallace as the lone forward in his side's 2-0 Coca-Cola Cup win over Darlington.
Speaking in the Yorkshire Post, Peterson said: "There is definitely a chance Tomas could play for Leeds again.

"He still has two weeks of his loan period at Zurich to go and at the moment he is probably not fit enough to play in the Premiership. But when he is finished at Zurich, Tomas and George Graham need to talk.
"It is up to them to talk about how Mr Graham wants the team to play. It is up to Leeds to talk about the problems Tomas has had at Elland Road. But no problem is so great that there is no solution.

"There is a new management team at Elland Road and there will be a lot of new players coming in. It is a completely new situation now and when Tomas finishes his spell at FC Zurich he needs to meet Mr Graham."
